paras: The whitecap notice to remove telephones from Black homes at Osyka and Magnolia was a demand, reported in January 1903, that the manager of the Cumberland Telephone Company in the two Mississippi towns take all telephones out of Black households. The manager refused and offered a $100 reward for the arrest of the senders, and a Jackson dispatch presented the notice as the latest act of a whitecap campaign it said was nearly over.

In January 1903 a Jackson correspondent described "whitecap outrages in southern Mississippi" that had dwindled to "occasional echoes." The dispatch linked the whitecaps with labor agents, saying that between them the result both had set out to accomplish had been brought about. It credited mass meetings of "law-abiding citizens" and several arrests with quelling the whitecappers in many communities.

According to the dispatch, the whitecaps' latest work was a notification to the manager of the Cumberland Telephone Company at Osyka and Magnolia to take all telephones out of Black houses. The coverage gives neither the date nor the wording of the notice, and the senders were not identified. The manager declined to comply.
The manager offered a reward of $100 for the arrest of the parties who sent the notice. No report of an arrest or of further action against the subscribers was found.

The story reached print as a special from Jackson in the Hattiesburg Daily Progress on January 20, 1903, under the headings "Is Practically At An End" and "Take 'Phones From Negroes." The Brookhaven Leader printed the telephone paragraph by itself the next day, and the Americus Times-Recorder in Georgia ran the full dispatch, datelined January 21, as "Whitecaps Are Quelled." Each version set the notice beside the burning of a Black man's home near Johnston Station.

The dispatch called the campaign "outrages" and praised the citizens who opposed it, yet it also treated the whitecaps' aims as accomplished and suggested only that it was "high time for both parties to quit operations." No coverage of the notice was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Whitecap notice to remove telephones from Black homes at Osyka and Magnolia
bases: The act was a notice from 'the whitecaps', part of what the dispatch calls the whitecap outrages in southern Mississippi, demanding that telephones be taken out of Black homes (A1).
All three reports carry the same Jackson dispatch in nearly identical words (A1, A2, A3); no independent local account or follow-up was found.

accounts.label: Jackson dispatch
accounts.gist: The whitecaps' latest work was a notice to the Cumberland Telephone Company manager at Osyka and Magnolia to take all phones out of Black houses; he refused and offered a $100 reward for the senders' arrest.

framing.detail: The Hattiesburg Daily Progress headlined the item 'Take 'Phones From Negroes' under 'Is Practically At An End', calling the campaign 'whitecap outrages' and praising 'law-abiding citizens', while saying the whitecaps and labor agents had achieved what both 'set out to accomplish'.
The Americus Times-Recorder ran the same dispatch under 'Whitecaps Are Quelled', and the Brookhaven Leader printed the telephone paragraph alone.

conflicts.note: Same text; the dateline differs only in the reprint. The date of the notice itself is not given in any version.
